q.t: Find the complement of 35° (in degrees).
q.e: Complementary angles add up to 90° (a right angle): 90 − 35 = 55.

q.t: Find the supplement of 110° (in degrees).
q.e: Supplementary angles add up to 180° (a straight line): 180 − 110 = 70.

q.t: When two lines cross, the vertically opposite angles are:
q.e: Each of them makes a straight line (180°) with the same neighbour angle, so both must be 180° minus that neighbour — equal.

q.t: The two angles of a linear pair add up to:
q.e: A linear pair sits side by side on a straight line, and a straight line is a 180° turn.

q.t: An angle of exactly 90° is called:
q.e: 90° is a quarter turn, the square-corner angle. Acute is less than 90°, obtuse is between 90° and 180°.

q.t: An angle greater than 90° but less than 180° is:
q.e: Obtuse angles are wider than a square corner but not yet a straight line.

q.t: Angles of 40° and 50° are:
q.e: 40 + 50 = 90°, and two angles that add to 90° are complementary.

q.t: All the angles around a point add up to:
q.e: Going all the way round a point is one full turn, which is 360°.

q.t: One angle of a linear pair is 65°. Find the other (in degrees).
q.e: Linear pair angles add to 180°: 180 − 65 = 115.

q.t: Two adjacent angles always share:
q.e: Adjacent means next to each other: same corner point, one common arm between them, and no overlap.

q.t: Which angle is equal to its own complement (in degrees)?
Which angle is equal to its own supplement (in degrees)?
The angles of a linear pair are in the ratio 2 : 3. Find the larger angle (in degrees).
q.e: 5 parts make 180°, so one part is 36°. Larger = 3 × 36 = 108.

q.t: Find the supplement of the complement of 30° (in degrees).
q.e: Complement of 30° is 60°. Supplement of 60° is 120°.

q.t: Two lines intersect and one of the angles is 70°. The other three angles are:
q.e: The opposite angle is also 70° (vertically opposite). Each neighbour makes a linear pair with 70°, so it is 110°.

q.t: An angle is 20° more than its complement. Find the angle (in degrees).
q.e: x + (x − 20) = 90 → 2x = 110 → x = 55. (Its complement is 35.)

q.t: Three angles on a straight line are x°, 2x° and 3x°. Find x.
q.e: Angles on a straight line add to 180: 6x = 180, so x = 30.

q.t: Find the complement of 62.5° (in degrees).
Four angles around a point are 90°, 120°, 60° and x°. Find x.
q.e: Angles around a point add to 360: 360 − 270 = 90.

q.t: An angle is twice its supplement. Find the angle (in degrees).
q.e: Supplement s, angle 2s: 3s = 180, s = 60, so the angle is 120.

q.t: An angle is 4 times its complement. Find the angle (in degrees).
q.e: Complement c, angle 4c: 5c = 90, c = 18, angle = 72.

q.t: Two supplementary angles differ by 48°. Find the larger angle (in degrees).
The supplement of an angle is 3 times its complement. Find the angle (in degrees).
(2x + 10)° and (3x − 5)° are complementary. Find x.
q.e: They add to 90: 5x + 5 = 90, so x = 17.

q.t: Four angles around a point are in the ratio 1 : 2 : 3 : 4. Find the largest (in degrees).
q.e: 10 parts make 360°, so one part is 36° and the largest is 4 × 36 = 144.

q.t: An angle is one-fifth of its supplement. Find the angle (in degrees).
q.e: Angle x, supplement 5x: 6x = 180, so x = 30.

q.t: A ray stands on a line, making angles (3x + 20)° and (2x − 10)°. Find the larger angle (in degrees).
q.e: They form a linear pair: 5x + 10 = 180, x = 34. Larger = 3 × 34 + 20 = 122.

q.t: The complement of an angle is two-thirds of the angle. Find the angle (in degrees).
q.e: x + (2/3)x = 90 → (5/3)x = 90 → x = 54. Complement = 36 = two-thirds of 54 ✓.

q.t: Two lines intersect. One pair of vertically opposite angles adds up to 150°. Find each angle of the other pair (in degrees).
q.e: Each angle of the first pair is 75°. Its neighbour forms a linear pair with it: 180 − 75 = 105.

q.t: What is the angle between the hands of a clock at 4 o’clock (in degrees)?
q.e: The 12 hour-marks share 360°, so each gap is 30°. From 12 to 4 is four gaps: 120°.

q.t: The supplement of an angle is 10° more than three times its complement. Find the angle (in degrees).
What is the angle between the bisectors of the two angles of a linear pair (in degrees)?
q.e: The two angles add to 180°. The bisectors take half of each, and half of 180° is 90° — always a right angle.

q.t: Two angles are complementary. One is 6° less than twice the other. Find the larger angle (in degrees).
What is the angle between the hands of a clock at 3:30 (in degrees)?
q.e: The minute hand is at 6 (180° from 12). The hour hand is halfway between 3 and 4: 90 + 15 = 105°. Difference = 75°.

q.t: The angles of a linear pair are (5x − 12)° and (3x + 16)°. Find the difference between them (in degrees).
q.e: 8x + 4 = 180, so x = 22. Angles: 98 and 82. Difference 16.

q.t: Lines AB and CD cross at O. ∠AOC = (4x − 20)° and ∠BOD = (2x + 40)°. Find ∠AOD (in degrees).
q.e: ∠AOC and ∠BOD are vertically opposite, so 4x − 20 = 2x + 40 and x = 30. ∠AOC = 100°, and ∠AOD is its linear-pair partner: 80°.

q.t: An angle is 30° more than half of its supplement. Find the angle (in degrees).
Five rays from a point make angles x°, 2x°, 3x°, 4x° and 5x° all the way round. Find the largest angle (in degrees).
q.e: 15x = 360, so x = 24 and the largest is 5 × 24 = 120.

q.t: For any acute angle, (its supplement) − (its complement) is always:
q.e: (180 − x) − (90 − x) = 90. The x cancels, so the answer is 90° whatever the angle.

q.t: The complement and the supplement of an angle are in the ratio 1 : 4. Find the angle (in degrees).
